title: Predictive and instructive cerebellar encoding of dopamine reward drives motivated behavior
title_zh: 预测性和指导性小脑对多巴胺奖赏的编码驱动了有目的的行为
abstract: To learn motivated behaviors, animals must both anticipate rewards and reinforce actions that yield them. Although cerebellar activity encodes natural rewards such as water and food, it also coordinates physical movements such as eating and drinking. To disentangle reward from consummatory movements, we trained mice to push for delayed dopamine (DA) rewards delivered directly into the brain. Here we show that cerebellar input streams use both predictive and instructive codes for DA reward. Two-photon imaging revealed that many cerebellar granule cells (GrCs) predictively encoded DA rewards with sustained activity that 'stretched' to match 1-second or 2-second delay intervals before terminating upon reward receipt. By contrast, most cerebellar climbing fibers (CFs) spiked just after DA delivery. In mice also trained with water rewards, encoding strength for DA matched or exceeded that for water. Both cell types contributed causally: chronic GrC inhibition disrupted self-stimulation learning, and CF self-stimulation 'rewards' drove moderate operant learning in naive animals. Thus, cerebellar encoding of DA reward helps drive motivated behavior, suggesting deeper cerebellar integration in brain reward prediction networks.
abstract_zh: 为了学习有目的的行为，动物必须预判奖赏并强化能够获得奖赏的行动。尽管小脑活动编码水和食物等天然奖赏，但它也协调进食和饮水等身体运动。为了区分奖赏与消费性运动，研究人员训练小鼠在大脑内推迟给予多巴胺（DA）奖赏时推动杠杆。在此，我们展示小脑输入流利用了对DA奖赏的预测性和指导性编码。两光子成像显示，许多小脑颗粒细胞（GrCs）预测性地编码DA奖赏，其持续活动“拉伸”以匹配1秒或2秒的延迟间隔，并在奖赏到达时终止。相反，大多数小脑攀爬纤维（CFs）在DA给药后放电。在也训练了水奖赏的小鼠中，DA的编码强度与水相匹配或超过水。两种细胞类型均起因果作用：慢性抑制GrCs破坏了自刺激学习，而CF自刺激“奖赏”在 naive 动物中驱动了中等程度的操作性学习。因此，小脑对DA奖赏的编码有助于驱动有目的的行为，这表明小脑在脑奖赏预测网络中具有更深层的整合。
